LESSON: READING 3.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: LIBRARY SKILLS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.2: Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading: Library skills

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading: Library skills. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we make use of the library resources well?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe key practices for effective library use
2. respond to texts related to the theme for information

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 3.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: LIBRARY SKILLS
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading: Library skills helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 3.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: LIBRARY SKILLS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Describe key practices for effective library use

What this means
In this part you learn to describe key practices for effective library use. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe key practices for effective library use.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading: Library skills”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe key practices for effective library use. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Respond to texts related to the theme for information

What this means
In this part you learn to respond to texts related to the theme for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respond to texts related to the theme for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading: Library skills to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respond to texts related to the theme for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading: Library skills is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading: Library skills”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: describe key practices for effective library use)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading: Library skills to a partner. (skill: respond to texts related to the theme for information)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading: Library skills to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe key practices for effective library use.
3. Practise this skill: respond to texts related to the theme for information.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading: Library skills from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading: Library skills: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading: Library skills?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we make use of the library resources well?
2. How have you engaged yourself in serving your community and society?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading: Library skills means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe key practices for effective library use.
5. Be able to: respond to texts related to the theme for information.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
